crackedness_criteria.name: Demonstrated Impact & Outcomes
crackedness_criteria.description: Evidence of delivering concrete results (metrics, shipped systems, revenue, growth, publications with clear contribution).

scoring_guide.high: Multiple clear outcomes with numbers or externally-validated impact; repeated delivery.
scoring_guide.medium: Some outcomes or impact statements, limited quantification or fewer strong examples.
scoring_guide.low: Mostly responsibilities, little evidence of outcomes or measurable impact.

crackedness_criteria.name: Technical/Domain Depth
crackedness_criteria.description: Depth of expertise shown via hard skills, research, systems shipped, technical leadership, or specialized domain mastery.

scoring_guide.high: Strong technical depth with credible complexity; advanced work, research, or systems ownership.
scoring_guide.medium: Solid skills and projects; moderate depth without strong evidence of advanced complexity/ownership.
scoring_guide.low: Surface-level skills list; minimal evidence of depth or difficult work.

crackedness_criteria.name: Leadership & Ownership
crackedness_criteria.description: Ownership, initiative, leading teams/projects, founder mentality, cross-functional influence.

scoring_guide.high: Repeated ownership/leadership; driving direction, mentoring, or leading teams/projects.
scoring_guide.medium: Some leadership signals (small teams, leading a project once), partial ownership.
scoring_guide.low: Mostly individual-contributor tasks with little initiative/leadership.

crackedness_criteria.name: Selectivity & Recognition
crackedness_criteria.description: Signals of selectivity/recognition (competitive programs, awards, fellowships, notable admissions, etc.).

scoring_guide.medium: One solid selective signal or several moderate signals.

crackedness_criteria.name: Communication Clarity
crackedness_criteria.description: Resume clarity: structure, crisp writing, scannability, and effective information density.

scoring_guide.high: Very clear, concise, well-structured; strong information density.
scoring_guide.medium: Readable but some clutter; moderate clarity issues.
scoring_guide.low: Hard to parse; weak structure; overly verbose or unclear.

fit_criteria.name: Fintech or Economics Domain Knowledge
fit_criteria.description: Measures direct academic coursework, research, or self-study in fintech, financial systems, economics, or related quantitative finance topics. Looks for evidence of formal training or deep independent engagement with the subject matter.

scoring_guide.high: Has declared economics major/minor, completed multiple fintech or economics courses, written research papers in the domain, or demonstrated deep self-directed study (e.g., publications, projects, certifications in finance/economics).
scoring_guide.medium: Has taken 1-2 relevant economics or finance courses, or has a tangential major (e.g., computational biology with economics electives) with some exposure to financial concepts.
scoring_guide.low: No coursework, research, or demonstrated knowledge in economics or fintech; background is entirely unrelated (e.g., pure biomedical or climate focus with no financial component).

fit_criteria.name: Fintech or Finance-Focused Project or Work Experience
fit_criteria.description: Evaluates hands-on experience building, analyzing, or contributing to fintech products, financial models, economic research, or startups in the finance/economics space. Includes internships, personal projects, hackathons, or research roles.

scoring_guide.high: Has interned at a fintech company, bank, hedge fund, or economic research institution; built a fintech product or financial tool; or contributed meaningfully to economics research with real-world application.
scoring_guide.medium: Has a tangentially related project (e.g., data analysis with financial datasets, a class project involving economic modeling) or a brief exposure through a club or competition.
scoring_guide.low: No discernible project or work experience connected to fintech, finance, or economics; all experience is in unrelated technical or scientific domains.

fit_criteria.name: Entrepreneurial or Startup Mindset in Fintech/Economics
fit_criteria.description: Assesses evidence of entrepreneurial thinking specifically applied to financial technology or economic problems — such as founding or co-founding a venture, participating in startup accelerators, or pitching fintech ideas.

scoring_guide.high: Has founded or co-founded a fintech/economics-related startup, participated in a fintech accelerator or incubator, or has a documented track record of ideating and executing on financial innovation.
scoring_guide.medium: Has participated in a general startup accelerator or entrepreneurship program (not fintech-specific), or has expressed clear entrepreneurial interest in fintech through clubs, competitions, or written work.
scoring_guide.low: No evidence of entrepreneurial activity or interest in the fintech/economics space; startup engagement is absent or entirely outside this domain.

fit_criteria.name: Quantitative and Technical Skills Applicable to Fintech
fit_criteria.description: Measures the candidate's technical toolkit (programming, data analysis, modeling, ML/AI) as it applies to building or analyzing fintech systems, economic models, or financial data pipelines.

scoring_guide.high: Demonstrates strong programming skills (Python, R, SQL, etc.) with explicit application to financial data, algorithmic trading, economic modeling, or fintech product development.
scoring_guide.medium: Has solid technical skills but application to fintech/economics is implied rather than explicit; could plausibly apply skills to the domain with minimal ramp-up.
scoring_guide.low: Technical skills are present but narrowly focused on unrelated domains (e.g., biomedical imaging, climate modeling) with no demonstrated or implied connection to financial systems.

fit_criteria.name: Engagement with the VC and Startup Ecosystem
fit_criteria.description: Evaluates the candidate's familiarity with and participation in the broader venture capital and startup ecosystem — including attending VC events, networking with investors, understanding funding stages, or working at a VC-backed company.

scoring_guide.high: Has worked at or with a VC firm, attended multiple investor events, has relationships with founders or investors, or has raised or sought funding for a venture.
scoring_guide.medium: Has attended a startup event or pitch competition, is a member of an entrepreneurship club, or has a basic understanding of the VC landscape through coursework or self-study.
scoring_guide.low: No evidence of engagement with the VC or startup ecosystem; no clubs, events, or experiences that connect to venture capital or early-stage investing.

metadata.focus_area: Fintech startups and economics — candidates are evaluated on their alignment with financial technology innovation, economic domain expertise, quantitative skills applicable to finance, entrepreneurial activity in the fintech space, and engagement with the VC/startup ecosystem.
